## 0925 Notes
reading a logged perdictor
 rent = b0 + 210 log(income)
 b reading: an 1% increarse in income goes about 210/100= $2.1 more rent
 y reading: it lets the mdodel bend, so it doesn't over predict rent in the richest tracts
 the rule: log x. keep y in dollars: b/100 = change in Y for a 1% change in X
 
the fold that broke
- one small district had all of its tracts in the test fold
- so the model was trained without ever seeing that level, and it cannot predict it
- fix: merge small groups before cross-validation

today: we put a number on the error / residual.
The spatial lag: my neighbors' average:
- coord <_st_coordinates(sales)
- w_knn <- nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k=5)), style = "W")
sale￥resid_lag <- lag.listw(w_knn, sales$resid)

Me v. my neighborhoods

equation: EEWij (Xi-Xmean)(Xj - Xmean)/Ei(xi-Xmean)^2

$$
\hat{\beta}_1 =
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(X_i-\bar X)(Y_i-\bar Y)}
{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(X_i-\bar X)^2}
$$

example: A 100, B 80, C 20, D -50, E -70
If Xmean = 16,
A*B (100-16)(80-16) = 5376
B*C (80-16)(20-16)= 256
C*D (20-16)(-50-16) = -264
D*E (-50-16)(-70-16) = 5676
sum = 11,044 *2 = 22088
sum2 = (84+64+4-66-88)^2 = 22,920

I n/EiEj*Wij = 5/8* 22,088/22,920 = 0.6
